results.text: The OCU400 DS is produced in HEK293 suspension cell culture using a production bioreactor-based manufacturing process. HEK293 cells are initially recovered and cultivated in an Erlenmeyer shake flask to initiate the seed train. The cell culture is expanded from the HEK293SF-3F6 working cell bank (WCB) and is performed through sequential scale-up of the culture volume. Following recovery, the cells are expanded through progressively larger shake flask cultures and intermediate seed expansion steps until the required cell biomass is achieved for inoculation of the production bioreactor. The upstream process is designed to support manufacturing across campaigns while maintaining consistent culture conditions and process performance. The upstream process flow for OCU400 production from GLP to PPQ scale is represented in Figure 3.

results.text: The purpose of the seed flask passage steps is to generate sufficient biomass of HEK293 cells for inoculation in the production bioreactor. Seed cultures are passaged at defined intervals under controlled conditions to maintain cell viability and growth characteristics. Subsequent seed flasks are inoculated at an appropriate viable cell density to support consistent expansion. Cells are sequentially expanded through culturing in a series of shake flasks and transferred to a seed bioreactor to generate adequate cell biomass for inoculation of the production bioreactor. The seed train strategy is scalable and designed to ensure consistent cell growth performance across manufacturing scales.

results.text: OCU400 is produced using the HEK293SF-3F6 Working Cell Bank (WCB), which is derived from a well-characterized HEK293 Master Cell Bank (MCB) established under applicable conditions. The Master and Working Cell Banks have been prepared, qualified, and fully characterized in accordance with regulatory expectations to ensure identity, purity, safety, and suitability for manufacturing use.

results.text: Following cell cultivation from the cell passage 2, an in-process sample is withdrawn for determination of cell density and cell viability. If the cell density and viability meet in- process specifications, a specified cell culture volume is transferred into an Erlenmeyer shake flask for further expansion. The cell culture is mixed with pre-warmed BalanCD HEK293 medium containing 2% L-glutamine. An in-process sample is collected prior to incubation for determination of cell count, viability and morphology. The flask containing the cell suspension were placed in a CO2 incubator for cultivation for a defined cultivation period.

results.text: The production bioreactor culture is collected into sterile centrifuge bottles and centrifuged for a specified time at 2-8℃ for harvesting. The cell pellet are resuspended with lysis buffer stored at ≤-60℃ for ≥ 72 hours. Frozen cell harvests are thawed in water bath at 37 ± 1 ℃ and treated with biolonase to digest host cell DNA and plasmid DNA. After conductivity adjustment with IEX buffer, the crude cell lysate is clarified by centrifugation and depth filtration and further processed using a 0.65/0.2-micron filter to reduce bioburden. The clarified lysate is purified using Capto AVB affinity chromatography in a bind and elute mode. OCU400 (AAV5-hNR2E3) is eluted at low pH, the eluate was concentrated by TFF (TFF-1) and further purified by density gradient ultra-centrifugation. OCU400 (AAV5- hNR2E3) is collected and concentrated to a designated viral particle concentration (Vg) by TFF (TFF-2) and formulated by diafiltration with the formulation buffer. An overview diagram for the downstream process is shown in Figure 4.

results.text: Density gradient ultracentrifugation with iodixanol is used to separate the empty capsids from full capsids. The TFF-1 concentrate is divided into multiple centrifuge tubes and centrifuged for 80 to 100 minutes. The tubes are punctured at the bottom, and an additional syringe is inserted at the top to force liquid downward. The first liquid portion of the tube is discarded, after which fractions are collected containing the full viral particles. These fractions are pooled from the centrifuge tubes and tested for Vg titer. The product is either frozen or used for the TFF-2 step for concentration and diafiltration using the formulation buffer.

Cell Passage 5: After 68 to 100 hours of cell cultivation, samples are collected from each flask and tested for cell density, viability, and morphology. The cell cultures obtained from cell passage 4 are transferred into six 3L Erlenmeyer flasks. Prewarmed BalanCD HEK293 medium containing (2% v/v) L-Glutamine (v/v) is added to each flask to make up final volume of 1728 mL. Prior to cell cultivation, 0.5 mL samples are collected from each 3000 mL Erlenmeyer flask and tested for cell density, viability, and morphology. The six 3000 mL Erlenmeyer flasks containing the cell suspension are placed in a CO2 incubator.

a. Pre-culture in 200 L Bioreactor:

While the Cell passage 4 is in progress, 50L BalanCD HEK293 medium is aseptically transferred into the 200L bioreactor. The bioreactor is run for pre-culturing and after 68 to 100 hours of cell cultivation of Cell Passage 5, a sample is collected from each of the 3L flasks to test for cell density and viability.

b. Inoculation in 200 L Bioreactor:

A feeding system is welded to the bioreactor bag and the pooled cell seed from passage 4 is inoculated to the bag using the compressed air. After 10-30 minutes of starting the culture, a sample is removed using a 50 mL sterile syringe for measuring cell density and viability.

c. First media addition:

After cultivation for 20 to 76 hours, if culture reaches the targeted cell density (1.0-1.6 x 106 cells/mL) and viability (≥85%), cells are fed with 25 L BalanCD HEK293 medium pre- warmed to 37±1℃. After 1 to 6 hours of culture, a sample from the bioreactor is removed for cell density and viability testing.

d. Second media addition:

After cultivation for 20 to 76 hours, if culture reaches the targeted cell density (1.6-2.0 x 106 cells/mL) and viability (≥85%), cells are fed with 25 L BalanCD HEK293 medium pre- warmed to 37±1℃. After 1 to 6 hours of culture, a sample from the bioreactor is removed for cell density and viability testing.

results.text: The production of OCU400 (AAV5-hNR2E3) is based on triple plasmid transfection in HEK293 suspension cells with transgene phNR2E3, pRep2/Cap5, and pHelper plasmids. The phNR2E3 transgene plasmid is designed, synthesized, and characterized for identity and integrity of various regulatory elements (AAV2-ITR, CMV enhancer, CBA promoter, chimeric intron from rabbit globulin gene, and SV40 poly A). The rep gene sequence consists of wild type AAV2 serotype, and the cap gene sequence consists of wild type AAV5 serotype. The pHelper plasmid is used to provide various factors for AAV5 production in HEK293 cells. During research and development, Ampicillin antibiotic cassette was replaced with a kanamycin antibiotic cassette in all the plasmids (phNR2E3, pRep2/Cap5 and pHelper plasmids) and characterized for identity in plasmids produced during cGMP production. The purified plasmids were released against the specification.

results.text: The frozen cell lysate generated from the cell harvesting step is thawed at 37±1℃. Following thawing, the lysate is transferred to a mixer bag. Samples are collected for Vg testing and frozen at ≤ -60℃. Biolonase is added to mixer bag at 400 U/g concentration. The lysate is then stirred at room temperature. Samples are collected from mixer bags after biolonase treatment and frozen at ≤ -60℃. Thereafter, an IEX buffer is added to the lysate, and the mixture is stirred to achieve the required conductivity. Then the mixture is centrifuged, and the supernatant fraction is collected. Samples are collected from the supernatant fractions for Vg titer and frozen at ≤ -60℃.

PBS (1X) is added to fill the remaining volume in the tube, and the tube opening is heat sealed. ✕ Tubes are centrifuged at 69,000 rpm for 80 to 100 minutes at 16 to 20°C. A hollow fiber filter is installed to the tangential flow filtration (TFF) system. A feed tube, retentate tube, and permeate tube are cyclically rinsed with WFI, determine the dead volume and perform integrity testing. The filter is cleaned with 0.5 M NaOH. The filter is then rinsed with WFI until the permeate liquid reaches close to pH of WFI. The filter is equilibrated with AVB equilibration buffer. The retentate tube and hollow fiber are drained and pH of permeate solution is determined (Table 30).

The Vg titer results of the eluate are recorded, and the eluate is concentrated to a target of 0.5 to 1 × 1013 Vg/mL Ultrafiltration is performed to concentrate the eluate. The retentate tube and hollow fiber are drained, and the permeation is collected in a SEBC bottle, and the weight is recorded.

The membrane is washed with AVB Equilibration Buffer, and the wash solution is collected in a storage bottle. Wash solution and concentrated virus particles are transferred into a storage bottle. Sample is collected and frozen at ≤ -60℃ for Vg titer testing. Final concentrated virus solution is stored at 2 to 8℃.

results.text:
After an initial WFI rinse, the Capto AVB column is sanitized with 0.5 M sodium hydroxide (NaOH) solution. The column is washed with a defined column volume (CV) of WFI followed by equilibration with defined column volume (CV) of AVB Equilibration buffer. AVB loading bag is removed from 2 to 8 ℃ storage and loaded onto the column at a specified flow rate.

The flow-through is collected in a storage bag starting at A280 of ≥10.0 mAU and ending at 50.0 mAU. Samples of the flow-through is collected for Vg titer testing and kept frozen at ≤ - 60℃. The column is re-equilibrated with a defined column volume (CV) of AVB Equilibration at a specified flow rate. The column is washed with a defined column volume (CV) of Wash Buffer, at a specified flow rate.

The viral particles are eluted with Elution Buffer into a SEBC bottle containing 2 M Tris buffer. Collection is initiated at A280 5 to 10 mAU and ending at A 280 20 to 10 mAU at a specified flow rate. The pH of the eluate is adjusted to 7.80 to 8.20 with 2 M Tris buffer (pH 9.00±0.05). Samples were collected from the eluate and frozen at ≤-60℃ for Vg titer testing. The remainder of the eluate is transferred to 2 to 8℃ storage. The column is washed with AVB Equilibration buffer followed by WFI and stored in 20% ethanol.

The filter is cleaned with 0.5 M NaOH and then rinsed with WFI until the permeate liquid reaches close to pH of WFI. The system is then equilibrated with DS Buffer (1.8mM sodium dihydrogen phosphate, 8.2mM disodium hydrogen phosphate, 180 mM sodium chloride, and 0.001% Poloxamer 188), pH of permeate rinsing solution should be 7.30±0.05.

Based on the result of the Vg titer test, the diluted viral particle solution is concentrated via ultrafiltration to the target viral particle concentration of 0.5-2.0x 1013 Vg/mL.

The concentrated viral particle solution is diluted 30 times with DS buffer, and diafiltration is performed for buffer exchange at a defined flow rate and TMP . The membrane is circulated with 1.0-1.5 DV of DS Buffer (wash volume for Phase1/2), and the solution added to the viral concentrate. Samples are taken for Vg titer testing and frozen at ≤ -60℃. The concentrated and purified OCU400 is stored at 2 to 8℃ for less than 24 hours.
